Package paint.shared.config

Class GenerateSquaresConfig

java.lang.Object
paint.shared.config.GenerateSquaresConfig
public class GenerateSquaresConfig extends Object
Holds configuration parameters used during the “generate squares” phase of the system. Values are loaded from a configuration file or preferences store, and if missing, sensible defaults are applied.

  • Field Details

    • WHOLE_SCREEN_MIN_REQUIRED_DENSITY_RATIO

      public static final double WHOLE_SCREEN_MIN_REQUIRED_DENSITY_RATIO
      Density ratio threshold for a 1x1 grid. With one square, the background is that square itself, so its density ratio is always 1 and would never pass the normal threshold.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • WHOLE_SCREEN_MAX_ALLOWABLE_VARIABILITY

      public static final double WHOLE_SCREEN_MAX_ALLOWABLE_VARIABILITY
      Variability limit for a 1x1 grid: effectively none. Variability is then measured over the whole image, empty areas included, and is not comparable with that of a normal square.

      A large finite value rather than infinity: the value is stamped into Recordings.csv, and the CSV writer formats infinity as "∞", which the reader cannot parse back.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • WHOLE_SCREEN_NEIGHBOUR_MODE

      public static final String WHOLE_SCREEN_NEIGHBOUR_MODE
      Neighbour mode for a 1x1 grid. Strict and Relaxed require a selected neighbouring square, which a single square does not have.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

  • Constructor Details

    • GenerateSquaresConfig

      public GenerateSquaresConfig()
      Constructs a GenerateSquaresConfig by reading appropriate keys from the PaintConfig under section GENERATE_SQUARES. If a value is missing, a default is applied:
      • numberOfSquaresInRecording: 400
      • minTracksToCalculateTau: 20
      • minRequiredRSquared: 0.1
      • minRequiredDensityRatio: 0.1
      • maxAllowableVariability: 10.0
      • neighbourMode: "Free"

  • Method Details

    • isWholeScreen

      public boolean isWholeScreen()
      Whether the grid is 1x1: one square covering the whole image, giving a Tau over all tracks. In that case Min Required Density Ratio, Max Allowable Variability and Neighbour Mode are not read from the configuration but fixed to the WHOLE_SCREEN_* values.
      Returns:
      true for a 1x1 grid

    • gridSizeFor

      public static int gridSizeFor(int numberOfSquaresInRecording)
      Converts a square count into a grid side length — the single definition of that conversion.

      It previously existed inline at four call sites in two different forms: some truncated with (int) Math.sqrt(n), others rounded with (int) Math.round(Math.sqrt(n)). The count always comes from a fixed dropdown (5x5 … 40x40) and so is a perfect square, which is why the two never disagreed in practice — but there is no reason to keep two formulas around waiting to.

      A non-perfect square can only come from a hand-edited configuration file. That still yields a well-defined grid, just a smaller one than was asked for, so this warns rather than fails.

      Parameters:
      numberOfSquaresInRecording - the configured number of squares per recording
      Returns:
      the number of squares along one side of the grid

    • getGridSize

      public int getGridSize()
      The side length of the square grid — i.e. sqrt(numberOfSquaresInRecording).

      This is the single place that converts a square count into a grid side. It used to be recomputed inline at four call sites, and not consistently: some truncated with (int) Math.sqrt(n) while others rounded with (int) Math.round(Math.sqrt(n)). The count always comes from a fixed dropdown (5x5 … 40x40) so it is a perfect square and the two agree — but there is no reason to leave two formulas lying around waiting to disagree.

      Returns:
      the number of squares along one side of the grid
